_cell_header.carries: How much of instruction precedence belongs to the MODEL, and how much to the SOFTWARE WRAPPED AROUND IT?
_cell_header.why_it_is_a_headline_and_not_a_footnote: Earlier drafts of this project called a harness-dominated result the boring outcome. That was wrong. If hierarchy is a property of the deployment, then reporting safety by model name measures the wrong factor. Published work already finds vulnerability moving by up to 47 points across configurations serving the same checkpoint.

the_three_renderers.plain_chat: Real chat-template roles. system / developer / user / tool are actual message roles.
the_three_renderers.xml_wrapped: Everything flattened into ONE user turn as XML-ish blocks. The transport role becomes a text attribute, not a role.
the_three_renderers.json_envelope: One user turn carrying a JSON context array. Same collapse, different serialization.

_cell_header.the_point_the_collapse_makes: In xml_wrapped and json_envelope the ACTUAL transport of every span is 'user'. What used to be a role token is now a claim inside text. That is not an artificial construction — it is what many production harnesses genuinely do. So each span here records actual_transport and claimed_transport separately, and the gap between them is the measurement.
_cell_header.replication_unit: The harness is the unit for harness claims. Three harnesses is n=3, however many thousands of trials run inside them. This is stated plainly rather than buried, because it caps how strong the harness claim can get.

Same claims as harn-02, different serialization. Any difference between harn-02 and harn-03 is pure format, with the information content held constant — a scale that moves when XML becomes JSON is a harness response surface, not a model property.

notes: The rank moved from a bracket tag on its own line into an XML attribute. Note this is BOTH a renderer change and a notation change — which is exactly why tier-10 exists to price notation on its own. Without that control this contrast would be uninterpretable.
Here the priority is a real JSON number rather than text. If declared tiers work better as typed fields than as text tags, that is a concrete, actionable finding for anyone building a harness.
